structural_proposals.title: Gap-up-day exhaustion arm: treat a significant intraday gap as a standalone qualifying condition, independently of prev_day_rally
structural_proposals.proposed_change: The current OR logic treats had_gap_up (gap_up_pct >= EXH_GAP_UP_PCT) as one of three alternatives to pass the rally gate. EXH_GAP_UP_PCT is not shown in the constants list, so its current value is unknown — but the missed sample shows DMART gapped modestly (prev-day +0.23%) yet fell 6%. Introduce a new constant EXH_GAP_UP_INTRADAY_REVERSAL_PCT = 1.5 and add a dedicated arm: if today_open_early is >= prev_close * 1.015 (i.e. opened up 1.5%+) AND the current price has already retraced below the VWAP of today's bars (computed on the 5m today_bars5 already available in the function), treat this as a standalone qualifying condition that bypasses the prev_day_rally / cumul_rally requirement entirely. Insert this check immediately after the existing had_rally / had_cumul / had_gap_up OR block, as a second OR branch: if not (had_rally or had_cumul or had_gap_up or had_gap_intraday_reversal): continue. The had_gap_intraday_reversal flag = (gap_up_pct >= EXH_GAP_UP_INTRADAY_REVERSAL_PCT) and (current_price < vwap_today), where vwap_today is computed from today_bars5 the same way it is in _screen_pdh_trend. This captures the DMART / HINDUNILVR pattern: stock gaps up, runs, then reverses through VWAP — a classic intraday exhaustion without any multi-day base.
structural_proposals.reasoning: DMART (gap_up_pct likely ~1-2%, fell 6.02%) and HINDUNILVR (actual_value=1.38%, fell 8.72%) are the clearest examples: neither had a 6% prior-day rally, but both showed intraday exhaustion. The existing had_gap_up arm should already help, but if EXH_GAP_UP_PCT is set similarly high, it also misses them. Adding a VWAP-cross confirmation to the gap arm makes it a structurally valid exhaustion signal rather than just a gap filter.
structural_proposals.expected_impact: Adds 2-4 signals per month in the earnings/news-gap-exhaustion category. The VWAP-cross requirement prevents firing on stocks that gap up and continue trending; only captures genuine reversal attempts.

structural_proposals.panel: Trap Reversal — Bear Trap (Bullish) and Bull Trap (Bearish)
structural_proposals.title: Replace paced-volume vol_ratio gate with a minimum absolute day-volume floor to prevent zero-volume expiries
structural_proposals.proposed_change: The panel has 12 Bear Trap signals and 9 Bull Trap signals in 30 days, with 0 wins and 20 out of 21 total signals expiring (never reaching T1 or SL). 'Expired' in this context almost certainly means the move after signal was too small to resolve the trade. The current reversal volume gate (TRAP_VOL_RATIO=1.0 vs avg_vol_before) can fire on very thin tape where the reversal candle beats a near-zero avg — passing a nominal 1.0x on 200-share bars. Add a new constant TRAP_MIN_DAY_VOL = 300_000 (3 lakh shares) and insert a check after the reversal_bar is confirmed: day_vol_so_far = sum(vols[:reversal_bar+1]); if day_vol_so_far < TRAP_MIN_DAY_VOL: continue. This ensures a minimum level of actual market participation exists before a trap signal is issued, filtering out the thin-tape false setups that produce 'expired' outcomes rather than clean wins or losses.
structural_proposals.reasoning: 21 signals in 30 days with 20 expiries and 0 wins across both directions is not a small-sample ambiguity — it is a systematic signal-quality problem. The most likely cause (given the reversal logic is structurally sound) is that the signals are firing on illiquid names or very early in the session when absolute volume is too low for the move to resolve. The TRAP_SPIKE_VOL_RATIO and TRAP_VOL_RATIO gates are both relative (ratio-based), so they do not catch cases where volume is uniformly thin all day. A floor on absolute participation addresses this directly.
structural_proposals.expected_impact: Reduces signal count by an estimated 30-50% (filtering the illiquid/thin-tape cases), but should convert a meaningful fraction of remaining signals from 'expired' to actual wins or losses — giving the panel real performance data within the next 30 days.

structural_proposals.title: Relax PDH_MAX_STRETCH_ATR from 0.5 to 0.75 and widen PDH_RSI_MIN from 60 to 55 to generate sufficient signal volume for statistical evaluation
structural_proposals.proposed_change: Only 2 PDH Breakout signals fired in 30 days (1 loss, 1 expired, 0 wins). This is not enough data to evaluate or improve the panel — the filter stack is too tight to produce signals. The two most likely culprits based on the code: (1) PDH_MAX_STRETCH_ATR=0.5 rejects any entry more than half a daily ATR above PDH — on a trending day this eliminates real breakouts that ran before the screener polled; raise to 0.75. (2) PDH_RSI_MIN=60.0 on the daily requires already-strong momentum AND a fresh PDH break — on most days RSI 55-60 is the zone where the breakout is just beginning, not already extended; lower to 55.0. Both changes together are conservative loosening, not abandonment of the momentum filter. Insert as direct value substitutions; no structural code change required. New constant names: keep PDH_RSI_MIN=55.0 and PDH_MAX_STRETCH_ATR=0.75.
structural_proposals.reasoning: 2 total signals in 30 days gives 0% useful win-rate data. The panel cannot be improved without signals to evaluate. The stretch and RSI gates are the most likely culprits because they are applied after the 200 EMA and VWAP gates (which are broad enough to pass many stocks), meaning they are the marginal filters cutting signal count to near-zero. There is no performance data to ground this more precisely — the confidence is therefore LOW and the change should be treated as a 30-day data-gathering exercise.
structural_proposals.expected_impact: Target: 5-10 signals per 30-day window to generate meaningful win-rate statistics. If win rate at the relaxed thresholds is still 0%, the panel concept requires fundamental review.

structural_proposals.title: Add a Nifty-direction gate for the bearish side: block Momentum Breakdown signals when Nifty 50 daily change > +0.5%
structural_proposals.proposed_change: The bearish Momentum Breakdown panel has 0 wins, 3 losses, 4 expired across 7 signals. The existing nifty_chg gate only blocks bearish signals when nifty_chg > 1.0% — it allows bearish signals in a modestly up market (+0.5% to +1.0%). Add a new constant MB_BEAR_NIFTY_MAX_CHG = 0.5 and change the bearish nifty_chg check from 'if nifty_chg > 1.0' to 'if nifty_chg > MB_BEAR_NIFTY_MAX_CHG' for the bearish direction only (leave the bullish side using the existing 1.0% gate). This sits in the existing nifty_alignment check block, applied only when not bullish. The bullish side's gate remains unchanged (block if nifty_chg < -1.0).
structural_proposals.reasoning: Momentum Breakdown Bearish: 0 wins in 7 signals. The most structurally likely explanation for a systematic 0% bearish win rate is market direction: if the 30-day window was broadly bullish (consistent with the PDH Breakout Bullish panel producing signals at all), PDL breakdowns that fire in a rising market are fighting the primary trend even within individual stocks. The current 1.0% Nifty gate is too permissive for the bearish side — a +0.7% Nifty day is a bullish tape and bearish breakdown setups in that environment tend to reverse quickly (explaining the 4 'expired' outcomes: moved down briefly then recovered). Tightening to 0.5% costs some bearish signal volume but biases remaining signals to genuinely weak-tape days.
structural_proposals.expected_impact: Reduces bearish Momentum Breakdown signals by an estimated 20-40%; should improve win rate from 0% by filtering the 'fighting the trend' setups. Small sample caveat applies — reassess after 30 more days.
